title: Halo Health - Postmortem & Reliability Follow-up
summary: Postmortem follow-up for the 2027-10-01 production incident where KV-cache invalidation during a model variant rollout caused latency spikes and 5xx errors for Halo Health. Reviewed root causes, mitigations already applied, and next steps: final postmortem doc, KV-cache benchmark, dedicated staging soak, and production rollout plan with added alerts and canary gating.
next_steps: Share final postmortem doc and remediation timeline by 2027-10-08 (Redwood)
Run targeted KV-cache benchmark with Halo production prompts (Redwood SE) by 2027-10-12
Provision dedicated staging capacity for Halo for one-week soak test (Ops) by 2027-10-11
Schedule follow-up sync to review soak results and decide rollout plan on 2027-10-19
action_items: Daniel Kim: run KV-cache + prefix caching benchmark and share results (due: 2027-10-12)
Rhea Banerjee (CSM): compile incident timeline and final postmortem doc and send to Halo (due: 2027-10-08)
Halo - Ravi Singh: provide 48h of production request logs and repro prompts for SE benchmark (due: 2027-10-09)
Sofia Patel: provision one-week dedicated staging capacity and test credentials (due: 2027-10-11)
meeting_header: Date: 2027-10-05 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 50 min | Attendees: Sofia Patel, Daniel Kim, Rhea Banerjee (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Ravi Singh, Liam O'Neill (Halo)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining — we wanted to do a quick follow-up on the incident from Friday the 1st, recap what we rolled back and what permanent fixes look like. Maya, do you want to kick off with impact from your side?
[00:18] Maya Chen: Yeah thanks, um so Friday afternoon we saw spikes in latency starting around 14:10 UTC and then a rise in 5xx errors about 14:22, it affected our appointment booking flow and about 12% of requests failed over a 30 minute window.
[00:35] Ravi Singh: to add, our SLOs were breached on p50 and p95, and users on East region experienced the worst of it. We also saw higher CPU on the inference hosts and some autoscaler thrashing.
[00:50] Daniel Kim: right — from Redwood's side we traced it to a model variant rollout that coincided with our KV-cache invalidation logic. There was an edge-case in the cache invalidation path when the runtime tried to swap quantized kernels for the new variant; that path cleared some prefix keys unexpectedly and created a cold-start storm.
[01:12] Liam O'Neill: Can you say that again? cold-start storm meaning all requests had to repopulate kv?
[01:18] Daniel Kim: yeah basically the KV entries for common prompts got evicted, so the next N requests missed the cache and caused increased compute and queuing; since the autoscaler policy was tuned for steady throughput it lagged behind, and the fallback to a lower-capacity model variant didn't trigger because of a routing policy mismatch.
[01:40] Maya Chen: We also saw a number of 503s from the gateway, some timeouts. The logs show connection resets during the peak.
[01:48] Rhea Banerjee: just to be clear, the immediate mitigation was rollback to the previous model variant and a throttled restart of a small subset of nodes, right?
[01:58] Sofia Patel: correct, we rolled back at 14:47 UTC, that brought latency back down within 7-10 minutes. We also temporarily bumped cache TTLs and raised our autoscaler thresholds to absorb the spike.
[02:10] Ravi Singh: do we have a confirmed root cause? is this a runtime bug or misconfiguration?
[02:16] Daniel Kim: it's a combination — an unintended behavior in the cache invalidation code path when switching kernel sets (so runtime bug), plus our rollout gating didn't catch the scenario because the canary size was too small and the metric was only error-rate not cache-miss-rate.
[02:35] Sofia Patel: the good news is we've reproduced the issue in staging with a targeted script that simulates a model swap while simultaneously invalidating prefixes. That reproduction helped Daniel's team make a patch.
[02:46] Daniel Kim: patch is merged into main; it preserves prefix keys during kernel swap and adds a validation step. We're preparing a hotfix build and a canary rollout plan.
[02:56] Maya Chen: what about alerts? We only noticed this once user reports started coming in — our internal SRE alerts didn't catch it early.
[03:04] Rhea Banerjee: we discussed new alerting for cache-miss-rate and sudden delta on kv hit ratio; is that still in the plan?
[03:12] Daniel Kim: yes, we've added a new metric and Grafana dashboard to track prefix hit ratio and a threshold alert that will page at 30% drop for more than five minutes. Also added a synthetic traffic probe that hits common prompt prefixes every 60s to keep hot entries warm during rollouts.
[03:33] Liam O'Neill: Synthetic traffic — will that affect cost? we are concerned about token spend for probes.
[03:38] Sofia Patel: it's a low QPS probe and uses cached responses only, should be minimal cost; we can also run the probes from your dedicated staging capacity to keep production costs down.
[03:50] Maya Chen: speaking of dedicated capacity, we want to discuss Dedicated vs Hosted for critical endpoints. If we had dedicated pools with pinned model versions would that have avoided this?
[03:59] Daniel Kim: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor and gives you predictable capacity and the ability to do isolated rollouts. It wouldn't have prevented the cache invalidation bug, but it would have limited blast radius because rollouts are isolated per-pool and autoscaling behaviors are separate.
[04:14] Ravi Singh: what about private deployment / VPC? Data residency and KMS are big for us. Any impact from the incident?
[04:21] Sofia Patel: not directly — this was runtime-level. However, for Private deployments you get more control over network topology and can configure your own KMS/HSM; we already support envelope encryption and customer-managed keys.
[04:34] Maya Chen: can we get the security docs and SOC2 artefacts? we need them for our compliance review.
[04:40] Rhea Banerjee: I'll send the SOC 2 and ISO docs and the KMS integration notes after the call.
[04:47] Liam O'Neill: good. On the roadmap for fixes — what's the timeline for the hotfix and the canary rollout?
[04:54] Daniel Kim: hotfix build is ready, we want to run benchmarks first. If benchmarks look good we'll canary to 5% of traffic over a rolling window next week and monitor prefix hit ratio and error-rate.
[05:05] Sofia Patel: action items captured: Redwood to run KV-cache benchmark, Halo to send logs and sample prompts, Redwood to provision staging capacity. Anyone object to the proposed dates?
[05:15] Maya Chen: dates look fine — just want clear rollback criteria for the canary.
[05:20] Daniel Kim: agreed, rollback triggers will be: >1% increase in 5xx, >20% drop in prefix hit ratio sustained >5 minutes, or any customer-facing error reports.
[05:33] Ravi Singh: can you put those triggers into the runbook and share? we also want a dry-run of the canary gating before live.
[05:40] Sofia Patel: yes we'll include runbook steps, rollback criteria, and who to page. We'll also schedule a dry-run during the soak in staging.
[05:50] Liam O'Neill: last question, any long-term reliability changes to prevent similar issues?
[05:55] Daniel Kim: long-term: hardened cache invalidation logic, expanded canary metrics (cache-miss-rate), mandatory synthetic probes for critical customers, better autoscaler tuning guidelines, and a playbook for prefix-aware rollouts. We're also evaluating an enhancement to the routing policy so fallbacks are triggered by cache-miss spikes.
[06:18] Rhea Banerjee: noted — I'll include those in the postmortem doc and label as short/medium/long term.
[06:24] Sofia Patel: ok let's recap next steps quickly — Redwood sends postmortem + runbook by Oct 8, SE will run benchmarks and share by Oct 12, Halo provides logs by Oct 9, staging provisioned by Oct 11, follow-up sync Oct 19. Thanks everyone.
[06:40] Maya Chen: thanks all, appreciate the quick response and the follow-up plan.
[06:45] Sofia Patel: thanks folks, we'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite for Oct 19.
[06:52] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (some punctuation and proper noun errors). References: shared artifact links — final postmortem doc (link: https://redwood.app/docs/halo-postmortem), KV-benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/halo-kv-benchmark).

Immediate mitigations (rollback, TTL bump, autoscaler threshold)
Short-term fixes (hotfix, canary rollout, new alerts)
Long-term reliability improvements and routing/fallback policy changes
Compliance documents (SOC2, KMS) and next steps
